## Overview Adds `tools/vllm-simulator`, the simulator half of RFC #61406. It runs the real vLLM v1 engine on a CPU-only host and bypasses model forward. A simulation clock then advances by a hardware-aware per-step latency prediction. The output is the same set of metrics `vllm bench serve` reports, for a target model, accelerator, and parallel configuration. This PR is fully independent of the CPU-based CI PR (#61407) and modifies no file outside `tools/vllm-simulator`. Once #61407 lands, the simulator can be simplified on top of it: its own mock platform and model-runner stub can be replaced, and real parallel ranks become possible. See [Relationship to the CPU-based CI PR](#relationship-to-the-cpu-based-ci-pr). The simulator is built by the same team, and with the same design, as the SGLang simulator (sgl-project/sglang#21891). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Maintainer decisions needed:** where the simulator should live, and which engine seams it may hook. See [Decisions requested](#decisions-requested). ## Claims - **Transparent to users.** Serving and the local engine API accept the same arguments and expose the same interfaces as `vllm serve`, `vllm bench serve`, and `AsyncLLM`. - **Zero changes to vLLM.** All 56 files are under `tools/vllm-simulator`, of which the core vLLM hooks (`src/vllm_simulator/simulation/vllm`) account for 1428 lines. Request admission, scheduling, prefix caching, block allocation, and KV-connector bookkeeping run on unmodified vLLM code. - **Two clock modes.** `NON_BLOCKING` (default) advances a virtual clock. `BLOCKING` sleeps for the predicted latency, so the server can stand in for a real deployment in real time. - **Pluggable predictors:** [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator) (default), replay table, sklearn model, and linear model. See [Predictors](#predictors). - **Topologies:** multi-instance with load balancing, and PD disaggregation through the native `DecodeBenchConnector`. - **Baseline collector.** Exports per-iteration batch composition and latency from real GPUs, for replay tables, ML predictor training, and accuracy validation. ## Validation **Functional tests.** Run on a CPU-only host with no CUDA runtime, against the [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator) `SOL` database for a simulated B300. Models cover the main attention and KV-cache layouts: - dense GQA: Qwen3-8B; - hybrid full attention + Gated DeltaNet: Qwen3.5-27B; - sparse MLA (DSA): GLM-5; - hybrid MLA + KDA: Kimi-K3; - compressed sparse MLA: DeepSeek-V4-Pro. ```bash cd tools/vllm-simulator && pip install . for t in test/test_simulation_*.py; do python -m pytest "$t" -v -s; done ``` | Test | Coverage | Result | |---|---|---| | `test_prefix_cache_and_offload` | All models above: device prefix-cache hit, CPU-offload hit after eviction, cache flush | PASSED | | `test_vllm_serving_blocking` | OpenAI server, `BLOCKING` | PASSED | | `test_vllm_serving_non_blocking` | OpenAI server, `NON_BLOCKING`, `bench_serving` client | PASSED | | `test_benchmark_round_robin` | 3 engines, round-robin routing | PASSED | | `test_pd_disagg_benchmark` | 1P + 1D, merged TTFT across instances | PASSED | **Large-scale deployment test.** A one-hour workload on the prefill instances of a large-scale PD-disaggregated test deployment was replayed in the simulator: 60 prefill instances, behind cache-aware routing, with an external prefix cache (KV connector to an external KV store) enabled. | Metric (1 h mean) | Simulation | Real | Difference | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Request rate (RPS) | 168.29 | 168.25 | +0.02% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 478.35 | 518.23 | −7.7% | | Cache hit ratio (%) | 77.25 | 77.86 | −0.61 pp | - **Request rate** matches by construction, because arrivals are replayed from the trace. - **Cache hit ratio** follows the per-minute fluctuations within about 1 pp. - **TTFT** tracks the real trend but stays consistently lower. That is the same direction as the unmodelled engine residual listed under [Limitations](#limitations). ## Details ### Why hooks instead of in-tree changes The primary goal is a workflow that is transparent to users. | Workflow | Real | Simulated | |---|---|---| | Serving | `vllm serve` | `python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server` | | Benchmark | `vllm bench serve` | `python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving` | | Local engine | `AsyncLLM.generate` | same code, after `init_hook()` | Arguments, request formats, and output metrics are unchanged. The entry point can also stay unchanged by installing the hooks from a startup file, either a [`.pth` import line](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#path-extensions-pth-files) or, on Python ≥ 3.15, a [`.start` entry point](https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#startup-entry-points-start-files). Such a file would need an environment-variable gate, and this PR does not ship one. An in-tree implementation would spread non-serving changes across `vllm/`: - arrival replay; - a virtual clock; - stats export; - a device-less platform and model runner; - no-op connector transfers. Each of these would add branches to hot paths. Hooks keep all of them in `tools/vllm-simulator`. They are installed at class-definition time, before vLLM is imported. **Maintenance cost.** Keeping the hooks outside `vllm/` does not make them free to maintain. The cost depends on how close each hook sits to low-level code, and the hooks fall into two kinds: - **`wrapped_*` functions** keep the native call and only add simulation state around it: arrival replay, the clock, and stats. They sit on engine-level interfaces (`EngineArgs`, `EngineCore`, `UniProcExecutor`) that rarely change. - **`override_*` functions** replace native behavior, almost entirely to remove hardware dependencies: device initialization, memory profiling, pinned buffers, and transfers. Together with the mock platform and the model-runner stub, these are the hooks most tightly coupled to low-level code. That is exactly the layer meta-CI (#61407) covers in-tree, alongside the code it depends on. Once #61407 lands, these hooks can be removed, leaving only the stable `wrapped_*` interfaces. Hooks also apply to modules outside vLLM. External components, such as KV stores with their own capacity management, can therefore be brought into the simulation directly instead of waiting for each one to add simulation support. ### Design - **Engine core.** `EngineCore.add_request` parks requests until the clock reaches their logical `created_time`. `UniProcExecutor.execute_model` converts each `SchedulerOutput` into `(scheduled tokens, past KV length)` pairs, queries the predictor, and advances the clock. `EngineCore.profile` dumps per-request and per-iteration stats. - **Worker.** A stub stands in for Model Runner V2. The KV-cache spec comes from a meta-device model walk under the simulated TP size and accelerator architecture. The KV budget comes from the target accelerator's HBM. - **Connectors.** KV offload and PD transfers complete immediately, so scheduler-side hits behave normally. ### Predictors Each predictor maps one step's batch, a list of `(scheduled tokens, past KV length)` pairs, to a latency. The predictor is selected by `predictor.name` in the simulator config. | Predictor | Source of latency | Typical use | |---|---|---| | `aiconfigurator` (default) | [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator) per-operator performance model for the target model, accelerator, and TP/EP size. Database modes: `SILICON` (measured kernels), `HYBRID`, `EMPIRICAL`, `SOL`, `SOL_FULL` (speed-of-light). | Hardware that is not available locally; capacity planning | | `replay` | Real per-iteration latencies exported by the baseline collector, matched by exact batch composition, with optional KNN interpolation on misses | Debugging by separating predictor error from scheduler and cache behavior | | `ml` | sklearn regressor trained on collector exports, over batch-composition features | A deployed model and accelerator with collected baselines | | `linear` | `base_ms + per_token_ms × scheduled tokens`; a constant step latency when `per_token_ms = 0` | Debugging | ### Relationship to the CPU-based CI PR The two efforts are independent by nature. - **Origin of meta-CI.** #61407 grew out of discussions in which functional CI also turned out to need CPU execution. It is in-tree because it goes deeper than the simulator: execution reaches model forward and runs fake kernels through their full lifecycle. - **What the simulator gains.** The simulator never executes model forward. For it, meta-CI only reduces the CPU-execution support it has to carry itself. - **Plan.** #61407 is not merged and may still change, so this PR ships its own minimal mock platform and model-runner stub. Once meta-CI lands, a follow-up will drop the `override_*` hooks, simplify the model runner, and allow real TP/EP/PP ranks. The `wrapped_*` hooks and the out-of-tree approach stay as they are. ### Decisions requested 1. **Location and ownership.** Is `tools/vllm-simulator` acceptable as a separately installed package with its own dependencies? 2. **Hooked seams.** The hooks cover `EngineArgs`, `EngineCore`, `Scheduler`, `UniProcExecutor`, `Worker`, the platform, and three KV-connector workers. Should any of these become narrow public extension points, such as a request-arrival hook or a step-latency callback? ### Limitations - **Version coupling.** A hook that fails to apply logs a warning, so a renamed method can degrade silently. - **Accuracy.** Only the comparison above is reported. `NON_BLOCKING` does not model the ~2.5 ms/step engine residual. - **Scope.** Text generation only, on Model Runner V2, eager mode, synchronous scheduling. Parallelism is modelled by the predictor only. - **KV cache transfer.** Transfer time is not modelled yet, for either external prefix cache loads and stores or PD prefill-to-decode transfers. Both complete instantaneously, so only the hit and miss decisions are simulated. Transfer models are follow-up work. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

@@ -0,0 +1,205 @@
+# vllm_simulator
+## Background
+As large language models (LLMs) are rapidly deployed at scale for inference services, inference performance directly impacts user experience, service cost, and resource efficiency. Key metrics such as Time to First Token (TTFT), Time Per Output Token (TPOT), and system throughput are highly dependent on the complex interplay among model architecture, hardware platforms (e.g., A100/H100/B300), inference engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM), and runtime configurations (e.g., quantization, batching, and parallelism strategies).
+
+Traditional end-to-end stress testing on real GPU clusters is expensive and time-consuming, making it impractical to efficiently explore the vast space of configuration combinations. To address this, we propose **vllm_simulator**, a high-fidelity CPU-based simulation system. vllm_simulator enables fast, low-cost, and high-fidelity prediction of key performance metrics across different models, target hardware, and configurations by replaying real-world inference workload traces collected from production or representative scenarios, thereby accelerating the design and optimization of inference systems.
+
+---
+## Introduction
+vllm_simulator is a simulation tool that hijacks a local vLLM installation. It launches a mock inference service—an OpenAI-compatible API server driven by the hijacked vLLM engine—that accepts user requests via real-world trace replay or synthetic load generation using standard benchmarking scripts. vllm_simulator outputs performance metrics identical to those produced by `vllm bench serve`. See **Quick Start** for usage examples.
+
+---
+## Installation
+```bash
+cd tools/vllm-simulator
+pip install .
+```
+
+> **Note**: vllm_simulator hijacks the `vllm` package at runtime through class-level hooks, so a working vLLM installation must be present in the same Python environment.
+
+---
+## Quick Start
+### Step 1: Mock Simulation
+This example runs inference simulation using a synthetic random workload. You may also replay real-world traces (e.g., `--dataset-name timed_trace`).
+
+#### Launch the Simulation Server
+Run the following command from the project root directory (the folder containing this `README.md`):
+```bash
+python3 -m vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server \
+  --model "Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8" \
+  --sim-config-path test/assets/config_vllm.json
+```
+
+> **Notes**:
+> - Use `--sim-config-path` to specify the simulation configuration file, which is equivalent to the system environment variable `VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH`.
+> - The server accepts standard vLLM serving arguments (`--max-model-len`, `--gpu-memory-utilization`, etc.). Do **not** configure TP/EP parallelism here; see the `scheduler` section of the config file below.
+> - The simulator uses `/start_profile` and `/stop_profile` as benchmark round markers (dump + reset simulation stats). vLLM only registers those routes when a profiler is configured, so the EngineArgs hook internally defaults the profiler to `"cuda"`—no `--profiler-config` needed. It stays inert: the hijacked `EngineCore.profile` never reaches the real profiler.
+> - `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` defaults to `""` inside the simulator so vLLM's platform detection stays consistent with the simulated environment.
+> - The provided [config file](test/assets/config_vllm.json) is for testing. Adjust the accelerator and other parameters to match your actual deployment scenario for higher fidelity.
+
+#### Run the Simulation Benchmark
+The benchmark client is a hijacked `vllm bench serve` and accepts the same arguments:
+```bash
+python3 -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving \
+    --backend openai \
+    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
+    --model "Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8" \
+    --dataset-name random \
+    --request-rate 4 \
+    --random-input-len 1024 \
+    --random-output-len 1024 \
+    --num-prompts 10 \
+    --save-result
+```
+
+The client does not pace requests in real time. Instead, every request carries a logical arrival timestamp (`simulation.created_time`), and the server replays the traffic pattern against its (virtual) simulation clock. Add `--save-result` (optionally with `--result-dir` / `--result-filename`) to persist the result JSON with the simulation metrics.
+
+You have now completed an inference simulation using framework interception.
+
+#### Example Output
+```bash
+============ Serving Benchmark Result ============
+Successful requests:                     10
+Failed requests:                         0
+Request rate configured (RPS):           4.00
+Benchmark duration (s):                  1.15
+Total input tokens:                      10240
+Total generated tokens:                  10240
+Request throughput (req/s):              8.69
+Output token throughput (tok/s):         8901.74
+...
+=============== Simulation Metrics ===============
+Completed requests:                      10
+Simulated duration (s):                  2.53
+Output token throughput (tok/s):         4053.36
+Mean TTFT (ms):                          128.59
+Mean TPOT (ms):                          12.14
+Mean E2EL (ms):                          3431.84
+==================================================
+```
+
+> The "Serving Benchmark Result" block is computed from client-side timings and is **not meaningful** in simulation mode. The authoritative numbers are the "Simulation Metrics" block and the saved result JSON, which are aggregated from the per-request stats dumped by the server (via `calc_metrics`); fields such as `mean_ttft_ms`, `p99_tpot_ms`, throughputs, and KV-cache hit ratios in the result JSON are substituted accordingly.
+
+---
+## Usage
+### Mock Simulation (Inference Simulation)
+vllm_simulator uses **dynamic interception** to hijack the execution flow of vLLM, bypassing actual LLM computation:
+
+- **Platform / Worker**: stub CUDA operations and KV-cache allocation so the engine runs on CPU while preserving GPU deployment semantics. The model runner is replaced by a stand-in for Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` is forced; the V1 runner is not modelled).
+- **EngineCore** (`vllm.v1.engine.core.EngineCore`): holds requests in a future queue and dispatches them by `simulation.created_time`; records per-request queueing and prefix-cache hit stats.
+- **Executor** (`UniProcExecutor.execute_model`): accounts the predicted GPU span of each step (AIConfigurator prediction + sampler/logprobs compensation) and advances the simulation clock.
+- **EngineCore.profile**: `/start_profile` and `/stop_profile` double as benchmark round markers—each call dumps `request.jsonl` / `iteration.jsonl` to the output directory and resets the stats.
+
+Key environment variables:
+
+| Variable | Meaning | Default |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH` | Simulation config JSON (see below) | — (required) |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE` | `NON_BLOCKING` (virtual-clock replay) or `BLOCKING` (engine sleeps the predicted GPU span in real time) | `NON_BLOCKING` |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_DIR` | Where the server dumps `request.jsonl` / `iteration.jsonl`; the benchmark client reads them from here | `/tmp/vllm_simulator/output/` |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_MAX_DECODE_STEPS` | Force every request's output length | unset |
+
+The benchmark client and the server must share the same `VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_DIR`.
+
+- For supported launch options, run:
+  ```bash
+  python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server --help
+  ```
+- For benchmark options, run:
+  ```bash
+  python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving --help
+  ```
+
+---
+### Data Collection (Collector)
+The collector runs a **real** vLLM server on GPUs and records per-step and per-request traces, used to calibrate the simulator, train `ml` predictor models, and build `replay` predictor tables. It accepts the same arguments as the `vllm` CLI:
+```bash
+VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_OUTPUT_DIR=/path/to/output \
+python3 -m vllm_simulator.collector.launch_server serve "Qwen/Qwen3-8B" --port 8000
+
+curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/start_profile
+# ... send benchmark traffic ...
+curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/stop_profile
+```
+
+Only traffic between `/start_profile` and `/stop_profile` is recorded. `/stop_profile` writes `rank0.schedule_batch.jsonl` (per-step batch composition and latency) and `requests.jsonl` (per-request timing, KV hits and token ids) synchronously, overwriting the previous window. Under TP only rank 0 is collected.
+
+| Variable | Meaning | Default |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_OUTPUT_DIR` | Export directory | current working directory |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_EXPORT_TOKEN_IDS` | Export `input_ids` / `output_ids` | `1` |
+| `VLLM_SIMULATOR_COLLECTOR_EXPORT_GZIP` | Write `.jsonl.gz` instead of `.jsonl` | `1` |
+
+---
+### Configuration File Format (`VLLM_SIMULATOR_CONFIG_PATH`)
+The config file is a JSON file with three main sections:
+
+- **`platform`**: Hardware settings
+  - `accelerator`: GPU model (e.g., `"h100_sxm"`, `"b300_sxm"`) and `hbm_capacity_gb`
+
+- **`predictor`**: Time prediction module
+  - `name`: predictor type (`"aiconfigurator"`, `"ml"`, `"replay"` or `"linear"`)
+  - See the **TimePredictor** section below for details
+
+- **`scheduler`**: Parallelism and backend metadata
+  > ⚠️ **Note**: Multi-GPU parallelism (TP/EP) should not be configured at the framework level during server launch. Instead, specify `tp_size` and `ep_size` here; the predictor will simulate parallel execution overhead accordingly.
+  - `backend_name` / `backend_version`: the simulated inference engine and version, used to locate the matching AIConfigurator performance database (e.g., `"vllm"` / `"0.19.0"`).
+
+**Example Config**:
+```json
+{
+    "platform": {
+        "accelerator": {
+            "name": "b300_sxm",
+            "hbm_capacity_gb": 80000
+        }
+    },
+    "predictor": {
+        "name": "aiconfigurator",
+        "database_mode": "SOL"
+    },
+    "scheduler": {
+        "tp_size": 1,
+        "ep_size": 1,
+        "dp_size": 1,
+        "backend_name": "vllm",
+        "backend_version": "0.24.0"
+    }
+}
+```
+
+---
+## TimePredictor
+### AIConfigurator
+- Project: <https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator>
+- Parameters:
+  - `database_path`: (optional) path to custom operator profiling data
+  - `database_mode`: (optional) performance database mode, e.g. `"SOL"` (speed-of-light) or `"SILICON"` (measured data); defaults to `"SILICON"`
+  - `platform.accelerator.name`: device/system name; it should be one of those defined internally in AIConfigurator
+  - `prefill_scale_factor` / `decode_scale_factor`: optional calibration factors to adjust predicted latency
+
+**Example**:
+```json
+{
+  "name": "aiconfigurator",
+  "database_path": "path/to/aiconfigurator/data",
+  "database_mode": "SOL",
+  "prefill_scale_factor": 1.02040816,
+  "decode_scale_factor": 1.01010101
+}
+```
+
+### Linear
+Predicts every non-empty step as `base_ms + per_token_ms * scheduled_tokens`, bypassing any performance model (debugging). KV-cache length is not modelled. Set `per_token_ms` to 0 for a constant per-step latency.
+- Parameters:
+  - `base_ms`: (optional) fixed per-step latency in milliseconds; defaults to 0
+  - `per_token_ms`: (optional) latency per scheduled token in milliseconds; defaults to 0
+
+**Example**:
+```json
+{
+  "name": "linear",
+  "base_ms": 10,
+  "per_token_ms": 0.02
+}
+```

+    created_time: Optional[float] = None
+    queue_start: float = 0.0
+    queue_end: float = 0.0
+    output_length: int = 0
+    input_length: int = 0
+    local_kv_hit_len: int = 0
+    ext_kv_hit_len: int = 0
+    input_ids: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("i"))
+    output_ids: array = field(default_factory=lambda: array("i"))

+

+    start_timestamp: float = 0.0
+    end_timestamp: float = 0.0
+    forward_mode: int = 0
+    # List of tuples (req_id, extend_input_len, past_kv_len, output_len)
+    requests: list[tuple[str, int, int, int]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    iter_latency: float = 0.0

+# Data is collected only between start_profile and stop_profile.  Worker
+# and EngineCore may live in different processes, so each side keeps its
+# own collecting flag, toggled by its own profile() call.

+_COLLECTING_REQUESTS = False
+
+BATCH_INFOS: list[BatchInfos] = []
+
+REQUEST_INFOS: dict[str, RequestInfos] = {}

+# Timing uses CUDA event pairs instead of torch.cuda.synchronize(), which
+# would break async-scheduling overlap and skew the measurement.  Elapsed
+# time is read after vLLM's own sync (AsyncModelRunnerOutput.get_output),
+# so the hook never synchronizes by itself.

+class _EventTimer:
+    """A start/end pair of timing cuda events for one measured region."""
+
+    __slots__ = ("_start", "_end")
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+        self._end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+
+    def record_start(self) -> None:
+        self._start.record()
+
+    def record_end(self) -> None:
+        self._end.record()
+
+    def elapsed_s(self) -> Optional[float]:
+        """Elapsed seconds, or None if an event has not completed (guards a
+        rare race so it never crashes the engine)."""

+            return self._start.elapsed_time(self._end) / 1000.0
+        except RuntimeError:

+
+# Hands the execute_model (RPC-1) finalizer to the same step's sample_tokens
+# (RPC-2); one slot suffices since the two run back-to-back.

+def _finalize_on_get_output(output, finalize):
+    """Run ``finalize`` once vLLM has synced this step's output: inside
+    get_output() for async outputs, immediately otherwise."""
+    original_get_output = getattr(output, "get_output", None)
+    if original_get_output is None:
+        finalize()
+        return output

+    def wrapped_get_output(*args, **kwargs):

+            exec_timer.record_end()

+
+            if scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs:
+                prefill_timestamp = time.time()
+                for new_req_data in scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs:
+                    req_id = new_req_data.req_id
+                    req_info = REQUEST_INFOS.get(req_id)
+                    request = self.requests.get(req_id)
+                    if req_info is None or request is None:
+                        continue
+                    if req_info.queue_end == 0:
+                        req_info.queue_end = prefill_timestamp
+                        req_info.input_length = request.num_prompt_tokens
+                        req_info.output_length = request.max_tokens
+
+                        # The local/external hit split lives on prefill_stats.
+                        req_info.local_kv_hit_len, req_info.ext_kv_hit_len = (
+                            kv_hit_split(request, new_req_data.num_computed_tokens)
+                        )
+

+            if req_info is not None and EXPORT_TOKEN_IDS and request.is_finished():

+                    if request.prompt_token_ids is not None
+                    else array("i")
+                )
+                req_info.output_ids = array("i", request.output_token_ids)
+            return original_free_request(self, request, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        target.add_request = wrapped_add_request
+        target.schedule = wrapped_schedule
+        target._free_request = wrapped_free_request

+import builtins
+from types import FunctionType
+from typing import List, Union
+
+from vllm_simulator.hook.base_hook import BaseHook, _register_hooks
+from vllm_simulator.utils import get_logger
+

+
+CLASS_HOOKS: List[BaseHook] = []
+
+_builtins_build_class_ = builtins.__build_class__
+
+
+def _custom_build_class_(func, name: str, *bases, **kwargs):
+    for hook in CLASS_HOOKS:
+        if name != hook.HOOK_CLASS_NAME:
+            continue
+        module_name = None
+        if isinstance(func, FunctionType):
+            module_name = func.__globals__.get("__name__", "")
+        if module_name != hook.HOOK_MODULE_NAME:
+            continue

+        except Exception as e:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Failed to hook class [%s]. Error type: %s, message: %r",
+                name,
+                type(e).__name__,
+                e,
+            )
+        return target_class
+
+    return _builtins_build_class_(func, name, *bases, **kwargs)

+"""Online serving benchmark client for the vLLM simulator.
+
+Hijacks ``vllm.benchmarks.serve`` so that:
+
+1. The client never sleeps between requests; each request carries
+   ``simulation.created_time`` and the server replays arrivals from it
+   (see ``C_VLLMEngineCoreHook``).
+2. Reported metrics are aggregated by ``calc_metrics`` from the
+   ``request.jsonl`` dumped by the server's profile hook.
+
+Usage:
+    python -m vllm_simulator.simulation.bench_serving [vllm bench serve args...]
+
+Requires the simulator server (``vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.launch_server``),
+which uses /start_profile and /stop_profile as round markers.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+from typing import AsyncGenerator, Literal
+
+import numpy as np
+from vllm.benchmarks import serve
+from vllm.benchmarks.datasets import SampleRequest
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.manager import Envs
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.utils import calc_metrics
+
+
+# Same arrival model as ``serve.get_request``, but the cumulative delay becomes
+# ``simulation.created_time`` instead of a sleep.  Self-timed traces are shifted
+# so the first request starts at zero.
+async def override_get_request(
+    input_requests: list[SampleRequest],
+    request_rate: float,
+    burstiness: float = 1.0,
+    ramp_up_strategy: Literal["linear", "exponential"] | None = None,
+    ramp_up_start_rps: int | None = None,
+    ramp_up_end_rps: int | None = None,
+    self_timed: bool = False,
+) -> AsyncGenerator[tuple[SampleRequest, float], None]:
+    assert burstiness > 0, (
+        f"A positive burstiness factor is expected, but given {burstiness}."
+    )
+    if not isinstance(input_requests, list):
+        input_requests = list(input_requests)
+
+    total_requests = len(input_requests)
+    assert total_requests > 0, "No requests provided."
+
+    request_rates: list[float] = []
+    delay_ts: list[float] = []
+
+    if self_timed:
+        input_requests.sort(key=lambda r: r.timestamp or 0.0)
+        first_ts = input_requests[0].timestamp or 0.0
+        for request in input_requests:
+            delay_ts.append((request.timestamp or 0.0) - first_ts)
+            # No notion of RPS for self-timed traces, same as native.
+            request_rates.append(0.0)
+    else:
+        for request_index in range(total_requests):
+            # Reuse the native helper so ramp-up semantics stay in sync.
+            current_request_rate = serve._get_current_request_rate(
+                ramp_up_strategy,
+                ramp_up_start_rps,
+                ramp_up_end_rps,
+                request_index,
+                total_requests,
+                request_rate,
+            )
+            assert current_request_rate > 0.0, (
+                f"Obtained non-positive request rate {current_request_rate}."
+            )
+            request_rates.append(current_request_rate)
+            if current_request_rate == float("inf"):
+                delay_ts.append(0)
+            elif burstiness == float("inf"):
+                # Constant inter-arrival time in the infinite-burstiness limit.
+                delay_ts.append(1.0 / current_request_rate)
+            else:
+                theta = 1.0 / (current_request_rate * burstiness)
+                delay_ts.append(np.random.gamma(shape=burstiness, scale=theta))
+
+        # Cumulative arrival offsets from the first request.
+        for i in range(1, len(delay_ts)):
+            delay_ts[i] += delay_ts[i - 1]
+        if ramp_up_strategy is None and delay_ts[-1] != 0:
+            # Same total-duration normalization as the native generator.
+            target_total_delay_s = total_requests / request_rate
+            normalize_factor = target_total_delay_s / delay_ts[-1]
+            delay_ts = [delay * normalize_factor for delay in delay_ts]
+
+    for request_index, request in enumerate(input_requests):
+        # vllm_xargs is the only path into SamplingParams.extra_args; values
+        # must be scalars/lists, hence the JSON string.
+        overrides = dict(request.request_overrides or {})
+        overrides["vllm_xargs"] = {
+            **overrides.get("vllm_xargs", {}),
+            "simulation": json.dumps({
+                "created_time": delay_ts[request_index],
+                "total_request": total_requests,
+            }),
+        }
+        request.request_overrides = overrides
+        yield request, request_rates[request_index]
+
+
+# Replace client-side metrics with the simulated ones from ``request.jsonl``,
+# dumped on the /stop_profile that ``serve.benchmark`` issues before returning.
+# The client-side result is kept if the file is missing.
+_BASE_RESULT_KEYS = {
+    "duration": "duration",
+    "completed": "completed",
+    "total_input": "total_input_tokens",
+    "total_output": "total_output_tokens",
+    "request_throughput": "request_throughput",
+    "output_throughput": "output_throughput",
+    "total_throughput": "total_token_throughput",
+}
+
+# vLLM serve result name -> calc_metrics name.
+_LATENCY_METRICS = {
+    "ttft": "ttft",
+    "tpot": "tpot",
+    "itl": "itl",
+    "e2el": "e2e_latency",
+}
+
+# Simulation-only stats worth keeping in the result json.
+_EXTRA_RESULT_KEYS = (
+    "num_requests",
+    "input_throughput",
+    "mean_queue_ms",
+    "max_itl_ms",
+    "prompt_tokens_cached_ratio",
+    "prompt_tokens_local_cache_hit_ratio",
+    "prompt_tokens_external_kv_transfer_ratio",
+)
+
+
+def _load_simulation_metrics() -> dict | None:
+    """Aggregate per-request stats dumped by the server-side profile hook."""
+    stats_path = os.path.join(Envs.output_dir(), "request.jsonl")
+    if not os.path.exists(stats_path):
+        return None
+    with open(stats_path) as f:
+        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]
+    if not rows:
+        return None
+    return calc_metrics(rows)
+
+
+def _apply_simulation_metrics(result: dict, sim: dict) -> None:
+    for sim_key, result_key in _BASE_RESULT_KEYS.items():
+        result[result_key] = sim[sim_key]
+    for vllm_name, sim_name in _LATENCY_METRICS.items():
+        # Percentile keys exist only when selected via --percentile-metrics /
+        # --metric-percentiles; override the ones present in the result.
+        for stat in ("mean", "median", "std", "p90", "p95", "p99"):
+            result_key = f"{stat}_{vllm_name}_ms"
+            sim_key = f"{stat}_{sim_name}_ms"
+            if result_key in result and sim_key in sim:
+                result[result_key] = sim[sim_key]
+        # calc_metrics reports the median instead of p50.
+        p50_key = f"p50_{vllm_name}_ms"
+        if p50_key in result:
+            result[p50_key] = sim[f"median_{sim_name}_ms"]
+    for key in _EXTRA_RESULT_KEYS:
+        if key in sim:
+            result[key] = sim[key]
+
+
+original_benchmark = serve.benchmark
+
+
+async def wrapped_benchmark(*args, **kwargs):
+    result = await original_benchmark(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    sim_metrics = _load_simulation_metrics()
+    if sim_metrics is None:
+        print(
+            "[simulation] No backend request stats found under "
+            f"{Envs.output_dir()}, keeping client-side metrics. Launch the "
+            "server with a profiler configured so that /start_profile and "
+            "/stop_profile are registered."
+        )
+        return result
+
+    _apply_simulation_metrics(result, sim_metrics)
+
+    print("{s:{c}^{n}}".format(s=" Simulation Metrics ", n=50, c="="))
+    print(f"{'Completed requests:':<40} {sim_metrics['completed']:<10}")
+    for label, key in (
+        ("Simulated duration (s):", "duration"),
+        ("Output token throughput (tok/s):", "output_throughput"),
+        ("Mean TTFT (ms):", "mean_ttft_ms"),
+        ("Mean TPOT (ms):", "mean_tpot_ms"),
+        ("Mean E2EL (ms):", "mean_e2e_latency_ms"),
+    ):
+        print(f"{label:<40} {sim_metrics[key]:<10.2f}")
+    print("=" * 50)
+    return result
+
+
+original_main_async = serve.main_async
+
+
+async def wrapped_main_async(args: argparse.Namespace):
+    # Profile routes are the round markers, so profiling is always on.
+    args.profile = True
+    return await original_main_async(args)
+
+
+serve.get_request = override_get_request
+serve.benchmark = wrapped_benchmark
+serve.main_async = wrapped_main_async
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+
+    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser(
+        description="vLLM simulator online serving benchmark "
+        "(hijacked `vllm bench serve`)"
+    )
+    serve.add_cli_args(parser)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    serve.main(args)

+import asyncio
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.bench_config import BenchmarkConfig
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.request import GenericRequest
+
+
+class BaseWorker(ABC):
+    def __init__(self, name: str):
+        self.name = name
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    async def async_generate(self, req: GenericRequest):
+        pass
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    async def trigger_simulation(self):
+        """Round boundary: export this round's stats and reset them."""
+        pass
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def get_request_stats(self) -> list[dict]:
+        pass
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def get_iteration_stats(self) -> list[dict]:
+        pass
+
+    async def flush_cache(self):
+        pass
+
+    def shutdown(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class BaseBenchmarkRunner(ABC):
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
+        # Worker's name -> requests
+        self.lb_routing_records: dict[str, list[GenericRequest]] = {}
+
+    @property
+    @abstractmethod
+    def all_workers(self) -> list[BaseWorker]:
+        pass
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    async def async_benchmark(
+        self, benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig, requests: list[GenericRequest]
+    ) -> dict:
+        pass
+
+    def benchmark(
+        self, benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig, requests: list[GenericRequest]
+    ) -> dict:
+        return self.loop.run_until_complete(
+            self.async_benchmark(benchmark_config, requests)
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _assign_created_time(
+        requests: list[GenericRequest], benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig
+    ) -> None:
+        """Set custom_params["created_time"]: Poisson arrivals at
+        request_rate when ignoring the request timestamps."""
+        arrival = 0
+        for req in requests:
+            if benchmark_config.ignore_request_timestamp:
+                created_time = arrival
+                arrival += np.random.exponential(
+                    1.0 / benchmark_config.request_rate
+                )
+            else:
+                created_time = req.custom_params.get("created_time", 0)
+            req.custom_params["created_time"] = created_time
+
+    def _record_routing(self, worker: BaseWorker, req: GenericRequest) -> None:
+        self.lb_routing_records.setdefault(worker.name, []).append(req)
+
+    def get_iteration_stats(self) -> list[dict]:
+        result = []
+        for worker in self.all_workers:
+            iteration_stats = worker.get_iteration_stats()
+            for item in iteration_stats:
+                item["worker"] = worker.name
+            result.extend(iteration_stats)
+        return result
+
+    def get_lb_routing_records(self) -> dict[str, list[GenericRequest]]:
+        return self.lb_routing_records
+
+    def flush_cache(self):
+        async def _flush():
+            for worker in self.all_workers:
+                await worker.flush_cache()
+
+        self.loop.run_until_complete(_flush())
+
+    def shutdown(self):
+        for worker in self.all_workers:
+            worker.shutdown()
+        self._close_loop()
+
+    def _close_loop(self):
+        """Drain tasks left on the runner loop (e.g. AsyncLLM output handlers)
+        and close it, so they are not destroyed pending on a closed loop."""
+        loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop = self.loop
+        if loop.is_closed():
+            return
+        pending = asyncio.all_tasks(loop)
+        for task in pending:
+            task.cancel()
+        if pending:
+            loop.run_until_complete(
+                asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
+            )
+        loop.run_until_complete(loop.shutdown_asyncgens())
+        loop.close()

+"""PD-disaggregated benchmark runner for vLLM simulation workers.
+
+Mirrors vLLM's PD proxy flow: each request first runs on a prefill worker
+with ``max_tokens=1``, then on a decode worker with the original output
+length.  Decode workers must be configured with the DecodeBenchConnector
+(``kv_transfer_config={"kv_connector": "DecodeBenchConnector",
+"kv_role": "kv_both"}``) so the prompt KV is treated as already transferred
+and only the last prompt token is recomputed.  The transfer itself is
+modelled as instantaneous.
+
+Per-request stats only exist in each engine's ``request.jsonl`` dump, so the
+two phases are separated by a round boundary on the prefill workers: the
+prefill finish time read back from the dump becomes the decode request's
+``created_time``.
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import dataclasses
+import uuid
+from collections import Counter
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.request import GenericRequest
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.base_runner import (
+    BaseBenchmarkRunner,
+    BaseWorker,
+)
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.bench_config import BenchmarkConfig
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.benchmark.load_balance import (
+    LoadBalancingPolicy,
+    RoundRobinPolicy,
+)
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.utils import calc_metrics
+from vllm_simulator.utils.logger import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+class PDDisaggBenchmarkRunner(BaseBenchmarkRunner):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        prefill_workers: list[BaseWorker],
+        decode_workers: list[BaseWorker],
+        prefill_lb_proxy: LoadBalancingPolicy | None = None,
+        decode_lb_proxy: LoadBalancingPolicy | None = None,
+    ):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.prefill_workers = prefill_workers
+        self.decode_workers = decode_workers
+        self.prefill_lb_proxy = prefill_lb_proxy or RoundRobinPolicy()
+        self.decode_lb_proxy = decode_lb_proxy or RoundRobinPolicy()
+        self.prefill_lb_proxy.init_workers(prefill_workers)
+        self.decode_lb_proxy.init_workers(decode_workers)
+
+        self.request_stats: list[dict] = []
+
+    @property
+    def all_workers(self) -> list[BaseWorker]:
+        return self.prefill_workers + self.decode_workers
+
+    def _pair_request(self, req: GenericRequest):
+        """Pair a request with its prefill and decode workers."""
+        prefill_worker = self.prefill_lb_proxy.select_worker(
+            self.prefill_workers, req
+        )
+        decode_worker = self.decode_lb_proxy.select_worker(
+            self.decode_workers, req
+        )
+        self._record_routing(prefill_worker, req)
+        self._record_routing(decode_worker, req)
+
+        # Shared id joins the two engines' request.jsonl records.
+        req.custom_params["request_id"] = uuid.uuid4().hex
+        req.custom_params["prefill_worker"] = prefill_worker
+        req.custom_params["decode_worker"] = decode_worker
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _phase_request(
+        req: GenericRequest, total_request: int, **overrides
+    ) -> GenericRequest:
+        """Per-phase copy of a request.
+
+        ``total_request`` is the number of requests routed to the target
+        worker: NON_BLOCKING engines start dispatching only after receiving
+        that many requests.
+        """
+        custom_params = {
+            **req.custom_params,
+            "total_request": total_request,
+            **overrides.pop("custom_params", {}),
+        }
+        return dataclasses.replace(req, custom_params=custom_params, **overrides)
+
+    async def _run_phase(
+        self,
+        workers: list[BaseWorker],
+        role: str,
+        phase_requests: list[GenericRequest],
+    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
+        """Run one phase to completion and return its stats keyed by rid."""
+        await asyncio.gather(
+            *(req.custom_params[role].async_generate(req) for req in phase_requests)
+        )
+
+        # Round boundary: dump this phase's per-request stats.
+        for worker in workers:
+            await worker.trigger_simulation()
+        return {
+            item["rid"]: item
+            for worker in workers
+            for item in worker.get_request_stats()
+        }
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _merge_request_stats(
+        req: GenericRequest, prefill_stat: dict, decode_stat: dict
+    ) -> dict:
+        """Merge P/D stats as seen by a client of vLLM's PD proxy.
+
+        The client only receives the decode stream, so the first token
+        latency spans the whole prefill plus the decode instance's first
+        step; later token latencies are the decode instance's.
+        """
+        prefill_latencies = prefill_stat.get("gen_token_latencies") or []
+        decode_latencies = decode_stat.get("gen_token_latencies") or []
+        if decode_latencies:
+            gen_token_latencies = [
+                sum(prefill_latencies) + decode_latencies[0]
+            ] + decode_latencies[1:]
+        else:
+            gen_token_latencies = prefill_latencies
+
+        return {
+            "rid": prefill_stat["rid"],
+            "prefill_worker": req.custom_params["prefill_worker"].name,
+            "decode_worker": req.custom_params["decode_worker"].name,
+            "created_time": prefill_stat["created_time"],
+            "queue_start": prefill_stat["queue_start"],
+            "queue_end": prefill_stat["queue_end"],
+            "last_event_time": decode_stat.get(
+                "last_event_time", prefill_stat["last_event_time"]
+            ),
+            "input_length": prefill_stat["input_length"],
+            "output_length": decode_stat.get("output_length", 1),
+            # The prefix cache only matters on the prefill worker; the
+            # decode worker's external hit is the simulated transfer.
+            "local_kv_hit_len": prefill_stat["local_kv_hit_len"],
+            "ext_kv_hit_len": prefill_stat["ext_kv_hit_len"],
+            "gen_token_latencies": gen_token_latencies,
+        }
+
+    async def async_benchmark(
+        self,
+        benchmark_config: BenchmarkConfig,
+        requests: list[GenericRequest],
+    ):
+        self.request_stats = []
+        for worker in self.all_workers:
+            await worker.trigger_simulation()
+
+        self._assign_created_time(requests, benchmark_config)
+        logger.info(f"Created {len(requests)} PD disagg request tasks.")
+
+        for req in requests:
+            self._pair_request(req)
+
+        # Phase 1: prefill only (first token), as vLLM's PD proxy does.
+        prefill_counts = Counter(
+            req.custom_params["prefill_worker"].name for req in requests
+        )
+        prefill_stats = await self._run_phase(
+            self.prefill_workers,
+            "prefill_worker",
+            [
+                self._phase_request(
+                    req,
+                    prefill_counts[req.custom_params["prefill_worker"].name],
+                    output_length=1,
+                )
+                for req in requests
+            ],
+        )
+
+        # Phase 2: decode, arriving when the prefill finishes.
+        paired = []
+        for req in requests:
+            prefill_stat = prefill_stats.get(req.custom_params["request_id"])
+            if prefill_stat is None:
+                logger.error(
+                    "No prefill stats for request %s; skipping its decode.",
+                    req.custom_params["request_id"],
+                )
+                continue
+            paired.append((req, prefill_stat))
+
+        decode_counts = Counter(
+            req.custom_params["decode_worker"].name for req, _ in paired
+        )
+        decode_stats = await self._run_phase(
+            self.decode_workers,
+            "decode_worker",
+            [
+                self._phase_request(
+                    req,
+                    decode_counts[req.custom_params["decode_worker"].name],
+                    custom_params={
+                        "created_time": prefill_stat["last_event_time"]
+                    },
+                )
+                for req, prefill_stat in paired
+            ],
+        )
+
+        for req, prefill_stat in paired:
+            decode_stat = decode_stats.get(req.custom_params["request_id"], {})
+            self.request_stats.append(
+                self._merge_request_stats(req, prefill_stat, decode_stat)
+            )
+
+        return calc_metrics(self.request_stats)
+
+    def get_request_stats(self) -> list[dict]:
+        return self.request_stats

+"""Requests for the offline benchmark runners.
+
+Workloads come from ``vllm.benchmarks.datasets``; ``from_sample_requests``
+converts their samples.  Import those datasets after the simulator hooks are
+installed (i.e. after ``vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.vllm_worker``).
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Iterable, Optional
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.benchmarks.datasets import SampleRequest
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class GenericRequest:
+    prompt: Optional[str] = None
+    token_ids: Optional[list[int]] = None
+    input_length: int = -1
+    output_length: int = -1
+    custom_params: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
+    # Extra args used as API request parameters when sending the request
+    extra_args: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        if self.prompt is None and self.token_ids is None:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid Request")
+
+
+def from_sample_requests(
+    samples: Iterable["SampleRequest"],
+) -> list[GenericRequest]:
+    """Convert ``vllm.benchmarks.datasets`` samples for the offline runners.
+
+    A sample timestamp becomes ``created_time``.  Only single text or
+    token-id prompts are supported.
+    """
+    requests = []
+    for sample in samples:
+        if sample.multi_modal_data is not None or sample.lora_request is not None:
+            raise ValueError("Multimodal and LoRA samples are not supported")
+        prompt = sample.prompt
+        if isinstance(prompt, str):
+            req = GenericRequest(prompt=prompt)
+        elif isinstance(prompt, list) and all(isinstance(t, int) for t in prompt):
+            req = GenericRequest(token_ids=list(prompt))
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported prompt type: {type(prompt).__name__}")
+        req.input_length = sample.prompt_len
+        req.output_length = sample.expected_output_len
+        if sample.timestamp is not None:
+            req.custom_params["created_time"] = sample.timestamp
+        requests.append(req)
+    return requests

+        weights += op.get_weights()
+    # Count weights on a single GPU
+    weights /= perf_model.config.pp_size
+    framework_reserved_mem_gb = 1.4
+    rest_memory = (
+        scheduler_config.mem_fraction_static * device.hbm_capacity_gb

+def calc_metrics(requests: list[Union[RequestStats, dict]]) -> dict:
+    stat_fields = {f.name for f in fields(RequestStats)}
+    requests = [
+        RequestStats(**{k: v for k, v in req.items() if k in stat_fields})
+        if isinstance(req, dict)
+        else req
+        for req in requests
+    ]
+
+    ttfts = []
+    tpots = []
+    itls = []
+    e2e_latencies = []
+    total_dur_s = 1e-9
+    total_input = 0
+    total_output = 0
+    completed = 0
+    total_local_cache_hit = 0
+    total_external_kv_transfer = 0
+    queue_durs = []
+    for req in requests:
+        completed += 1
+        ttfts.append(req.gen_token_latencies[0])
+        queue_durs.append(req.queue_end - req.queue_start)
+        if len(req.gen_token_latencies) > 1:
+            # output length > 1
+            tpots.append(np.mean(req.gen_token_latencies[1:]))
+        itls.extend(req.gen_token_latencies[1:])
+        e2e_latencies.append(sum(req.gen_token_latencies))
+        total_dur_s = max(total_dur_s, req.last_event_time)
+        total_input += req.input_length
+        total_output += req.output_length
+        total_local_cache_hit += req.local_kv_hit_len
+        total_external_kv_transfer += req.ext_kv_hit_len
+    total_cached_tokens = total_local_cache_hit + total_external_kv_transfer
+    return {
+        "num_requests": len(requests),
+        "completed": completed,
+        "total_input": total_input,
+        "total_output": total_output,
+        "duration": total_dur_s,
+        "request_throughput": len(requests) / total_dur_s,
+        "input_throughput": total_input / total_dur_s,
+        "output_throughput": total_output / total_dur_s,

+        "prompt_tokens_cached_ratio": (

+        ),

+        ),

+"""
+Engine-core hooks that drive one simulated engine step:
+
+- C_VLLMEngineCoreHook: created_time-based request dispatch, BLOCKING-mode
+  request stats and profile()-driven stats export.
+- C_VLLMSchedulerHook: counts parked requests as unfinished so the busy
+  loop keeps stepping.
+- C_VLLMExecutorHook: inits the time predictor, accounts the predicted GPU
+  span at execute_model and records queue/hit, iteration and per-token stats.
+
+The hooks share the module-level request/iteration stats.
+"""
+
+import heapq
+import json
+import os
+import time
+from dataclasses import asdict
+
+from vllm_simulator.hook import BaseHook
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.manager import ConfigManager, StateManager, Envs
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.types import IterationStats, RequestStats, SimulationMode
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.vllm.utils import kv_hit_split
+from vllm_simulator.time_predictor import ScheduleBatch, ScheduleRequest
+from vllm_simulator.utils import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+# When set, overrides max_tokens (with ignore_eos) for every request.
+_MAX_DECODE_STEPS = int(v) if (v := os.environ.get("VLLM_SIMULATOR_MAX_DECODE_STEPS")) is not None else None
+_SIM_MODE = SimulationMode(Envs.simulation_mode())
+
+# Per-request stats keyed by request id; one engine per process.
+_REQUEST_STATS: dict[str, RequestStats] = {}
+# One record per forward step, appended by C_VLLMExecutorHook.
+_ITERATION_STATS: list[IterationStats] = []
+
+def _new_request_stats(request, created_time, queue_start, last_event_time):
+    """Initialize the RequestStats entry; hit fields are set at queue_end."""
+    rid = request.request_id
+    st = _REQUEST_STATS.setdefault(rid, RequestStats(rid=rid))
+    st.created_time = created_time
+    st.queue_start = queue_start
+    st.queue_end = -1
+    st.gen_token_latencies = []
+    st.last_event_time = last_event_time
+    st.input_length = request.num_prompt_tokens
+    st.output_length = request.max_tokens
+    return st
+
+
+class ReqDispatcher:
+    """Singleton holding the NON_BLOCKING replay state.
+
+    Requests parked at EngineCore.add_request are released by dispatch()
+    once global_clock >= created_time.
+    """
+
+    _instance = None
+    _initialized = False
+
+    def __new__(cls):
+        if cls._instance is None:
+            cls._instance = super().__new__(cls)
+        return cls._instance
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        if self.__class__._initialized:
+            return
+        # (created_time, seq, request, request_wave); seq breaks ties so
+        # requests are never compared.
+        self.future_queue: list[tuple[float, int, object, int]] = []
+        self.seq_counter = 0
+        self.total_expected = float("inf")
+        self.all_received = False
+        # Captured once at hook install (single engine per process)
+        self.original_core_add_request = None
+        # Live Scheduler, read by C_VLLMExecutorHook.
+        self.scheduler = None
+        self.__class__._initialized = True
+
+    def reset(self):
+        self.future_queue.clear()
+        self.seq_counter = 0
+        self.total_expected = float("inf")
+        self.all_received = False
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.future_queue)
+
+    def has_next(self) -> bool:
+        return len(self.future_queue) > 0
+
+    def next_req_created_time(self) -> float:
+        return self.future_queue[0][0]
+
+    def add(self, request, request_wave: int, created_time: float):
+        """Park a request fully inert until its created_time."""
+        heapq.heappush(
+            self.future_queue,
+            (created_time, self.seq_counter, request, request_wave),
+        )
+        self.seq_counter += 1
+
+        if self.seq_counter >= self.total_expected:
+            self.all_received = True
+            logger.info(
+                "All %d requests received. Starting simulation.",
+                self.total_expected,
+            )
+
+    def dispatch(self, engine_core):
+        """Re-submit due parked requests through the native add_request."""
+        current_time = StateManager.get_global_clock()
+        while self.future_queue and self.future_queue[0][0] <= current_time:
+            created_time, _, request, request_wave = heapq.heappop(
+                self.future_queue
+            )
+            _new_request_stats(
+                request,
+                created_time=created_time,
+                queue_start=current_time,
+                last_event_time=created_time,
+            )
+            self.original_core_add_request(engine_core, request, request_wave)
+
+
+class C_VLLMSchedulerHook(BaseHook):
+    """Count parked requests as unfinished.
+
+    The busy loop queries the Scheduler directly, so without this it would
+    go idle and never dispatch.  has_unfinished_requests / has_requests
+    derive from get_num_unfinished_requests.
+    """
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "Scheduler"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        original_get_num_unfinished = target.get_num_unfinished_requests
+        target.get_num_unfinished_requests = lambda self: (
+            original_get_num_unfinished(self) + len(ReqDispatcher())
+        )
+
+
+class C_VLLMEngineCoreHook(BaseHook):
+    """Created_time-based request dispatch at EngineCore.
+
+    Requests are parked in add_request, ahead of Scheduler.add_request, so
+    no connector lookup or block allocation happens before created_time.
+    step() dispatches them in created_time order.
+
+    Prefix block hashing still runs earlier in preprocess_add_request; it
+    touches no cache state.
+    """
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "EngineCore"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.engine.core"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        original_init = target.__init__
+        original_add_request = target.add_request
+        original_step = target.step
+        dispatcher = ReqDispatcher()
+        dispatcher.original_core_add_request = original_add_request
+
+        def wrapped_init(self, vllm_config, *args, **kwargs):
+            """Reset replay state and stats."""
+            ReqDispatcher().reset()
+            _REQUEST_STATS.clear()
+            _ITERATION_STATS.clear()
+
+            original_init(self, vllm_config, *args, **kwargs)
+            ReqDispatcher().scheduler = self.scheduler
+
+        def wrapped_add_request(self, request, request_wave=0):
+            """Park NON_BLOCKING simulation requests; forward the rest."""
+            if _MAX_DECODE_STEPS is not None:
+                if request.sampling_params is not None:
+                    request.sampling_params.max_tokens = _MAX_DECODE_STEPS
+                    request.sampling_params.ignore_eos = True
+                request.max_tokens = _MAX_DECODE_STEPS
+
+            created_time = None
+            sp = request.sampling_params
+            if sp is not None and sp.extra_args:
+                sim = sp.extra_args.get("simulation")
+                # JSON-encoded by HTTP clients (see bench_serving).
+                if isinstance(sim, str):
+                    sim = json.loads(sim)
+                if sim:
+                    created_time = sim.get("created_time")
+                    total = sim.get("total_request")
+                    if total is not None:
+                        dispatcher.total_expected = total
+
+            if _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.BLOCKING:
+                now = time.time()
+                _new_request_stats(
+                    request,
+                    created_time=created_time if created_time is not None else now,
+                    queue_start=now,
+                    last_event_time=now,
+                )
+            if created_time is None or _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.BLOCKING:
+                original_add_request(self, request, request_wave)
+                return
+
+            dispatcher.add(request, request_wave, created_time)
+
+        def wrapped_step(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            """Dispatch due future-queue requests before each engine step."""
+            if _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.NON_BLOCKING and dispatcher.all_received:
+                dispatcher.dispatch(self)
+
+                # Idle: jump the virtual clock to the next created_time.
+                if (
+                    not self.scheduler.waiting
+                    and not self.scheduler.running
+                    and dispatcher.has_next()
+                ):
+                    StateManager.set_global_clock(
+                        dispatcher.next_req_created_time() + 1e-6
+                    )
+                    dispatcher.dispatch(self)
+
+            return original_step(self, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        target.__init__ = wrapped_init
+        target.add_request = wrapped_add_request
+        target.step = wrapped_step
+
+        # profile() is the benchmark round separator: dump stats to
+        # VLLM_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_DIR and reset.  Merged here because only the
+        # first hook matching a class is applied.  The signature must match
+        # the native one: the utility RPC always sends (is_start,
+        # profile_prefix).
+        def wrapped_profile(
+            self, is_start: bool = True, profile_prefix: str | None = None
+        ):
+            req_stats = list(_REQUEST_STATS.values())
+            output_dir = Envs.output_dir()
+            with open(os.path.join(output_dir, "request.jsonl"), "w") as f:
+                for item in req_stats:
+                    f.write(json.dumps(asdict(item), default=str) + "\n")
+            with open(os.path.join(output_dir, "iteration.jsonl"), "w") as f:
+                for item in _ITERATION_STATS:
+                    f.write(json.dumps(asdict(item), default=str) + "\n")
+
+            logger.info(
+                "[ProfileHook] Exported %d requests, %d iterations to %s",
+                len(req_stats),
+                len(_ITERATION_STATS),
+                output_dir,
+            )
+
+            _REQUEST_STATS.clear()
+            _ITERATION_STATS.clear()
+            # Runs in the engine-core process, the only place this state is
+            # reachable under AsyncLLM.
+            StateManager.reset()
+            ReqDispatcher().reset()
+
+        target.profile = wrapped_profile
+
+
+class C_VLLMExecutorHook(BaseHook):
+    """Account the predicted GPU span at UniProcExecutor.execute_model.
+
+    ExecutorWithExternalLauncher inherits the hooked method.
+    """
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "UniProcExecutor"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.executor.uniproc_executor"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        original_init_executor = target._init_executor
+        original_execute_model = target.execute_model
+
+        def wrapped_init_executor(self):
+            # Worker.init_device (inside) resolves the ConfigManager state.
+            original_init_executor(self)
+            self._sim_predictor = ConfigManager.get_inference_time_predictor()
+            logger.info(
+                "%s initialized for vLLM.", type(self._sim_predictor).__name__
+            )
+
+        def wrapped_execute_model(self, scheduler_output, *args, **kwargs):
+            num_scheduled_tokens = scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens
+            if not num_scheduled_tokens:
+                return original_execute_model(
+                    self, scheduler_output, *args, **kwargs)
+
+            # Clock before this step is accounted.
+            queue_end_time = (
+                time.time()
+                if _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.BLOCKING
+                else StateManager.get_global_clock()
+            )
+            # Scheduled requests stay in Scheduler.requests until
+            # update_from_output.
+            requests = ReqDispatcher().scheduler.requests
+
+            # Pre-step num_computed_tokens, i.e. past_kv_length.
+            new_reqs = scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs
+            num_computed = {r.req_id: r.num_computed_tokens for r in new_reqs}
+            cached = scheduler_output.scheduled_cached_reqs
+            num_computed.update(zip(cached.req_ids, cached.num_computed_tokens))
+
+            for new_req_data in new_reqs:
+                # Resumed requests also arrive here (V2 layout); queue and hit
+                # stats belong to the first schedule only.
+                st = _REQUEST_STATS.get(new_req_data.req_id)
+                if st is not None and st.queue_end == -1:
+                    st.queue_end = queue_end_time
+                    st.local_kv_hit_len, st.ext_kv_hit_len = kv_hit_split(
+                        requests[new_req_data.req_id],
+                        new_req_data.num_computed_tokens,
+                    )
+                    logger.info(
+                        "[HitRate] rid=%s input_len=%d local_hit=%d ext_hit=%d",
+                        st.rid,
+                        st.input_length,
+                        st.local_kv_hit_len,
+                        st.ext_kv_hit_len,
+                    )
+
+            # token_emitted is False for intermediate chunked-prefill steps;
+            # passed to _ModelRunnerStub on scheduler_output.
+            simulation_batch = ScheduleBatch(reqs=[])
+            token_emitted: dict[str, bool] = {}
+            logprobs_tokens = 0
+            for req_id, num_tokens in num_scheduled_tokens.items():
+                request = requests[req_id]
+                past_kv_length = num_computed[req_id]
+                # GPUModelRunnerV2 samples nothing while seq_len < prefill_len
+                # (chunked prefill); num_tokens is prefill_len at (re)admission
+                # and seq_len - 1 while decoding.
+                token_emitted[req_id] = (
+                    past_kv_length + num_tokens >= request.num_tokens
+                )
+                sp = request.sampling_params
+                if sp is not None and sp.logprobs:
+                    logprobs_tokens += num_tokens
+                simulation_batch.reqs.append(
+                    ScheduleRequest(
+                        extend_length=num_tokens,
+                        past_kv_length=past_kv_length,
+                    )
+                )
+            scheduler_output._sim_token_emitted = token_emitted
+
+            result = original_execute_model(
+                self, scheduler_output, *args, **kwargs)
+
+            predictor = self._sim_predictor
+            predicted_latency = float(
+                predictor.predict_infer_time(simulation_batch)
+            )
+
+            # Logprobs cost missing from a baseline collected without them;
+            # active only with logprobs_cost_us_per_token > 0.
+            logprobs_latency = predictor.logprobs_cost_s_per_token * logprobs_tokens
+
+            # RPC-2 (sample_tokens) span, kept separate from the RPC-1-only
+            # predicted_latency so both stay auditable in iteration.jsonl.
+            total_tokens = sum(num_scheduled_tokens.values())
+            sample_tokens_latency = float(
+                predictor.predict_sample_tokens_time(total_tokens)
+            )
+
+            iter_stats = IterationStats(
+                requests=simulation_batch.request_info(),
+                forward_latency=predicted_latency,
+                sample_tokens_latency=sample_tokens_latency,
+                logprobs_latency=logprobs_latency,
+                total_tokens=total_tokens,
+            )
+            _ITERATION_STATS.append(iter_stats)
+            full_step_latency = iter_stats.full_step_latency
+
+            if _SIM_MODE == SimulationMode.BLOCKING:
+                # Engine CPU overhead is spent by the real loop; sleep only
+                # for the GPU span.
+                time.sleep(full_step_latency)
+                event_time = time.time()
+            else:
+                # Known diff, deliberately uncompensated: the engine residual
+                # (~2.5ms/step of RPC + EngineCore bookkeeping, outside the
+                # label) is not modelled, so NON_BLOCKING runs ~2.5ms/step
+                # shorter than real.
+                StateManager.step_global_clock(full_step_latency)
+                event_time = StateManager.get_global_clock()
+
+            for req_id in num_scheduled_tokens:
+                # Skip non-emitting chunks so the first latency is the full
+                # TTFT.
+                if not token_emitted[req_id]:
+                    continue
+                st = _REQUEST_STATS.get(req_id)
+                if st is not None:
+                    st.gen_token_latencies.append(
+                        event_time - st.last_event_time
+                    )
+                    st.last_event_time = event_time
+
+            return result
+
+        target._init_executor = wrapped_init_executor
+        target.execute_model = wrapped_execute_model
+        logger.info("[vLLM Hijack] UniProcExecutor hook installed "
+                    "(simulated GPU span at execute_model)")

+"""
+Worker-side hooks for vLLM's CPU offloading connectors.
+
+There is no data to move, so stores and loads complete immediately and the
+scheduler side sees host-cache hits normally.  Covers SimpleCPUOffloadWorker
+(VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1) and OffloadingConnectorWorker.

+class C_VLLMSimpleCPUOffloadWorkerHook(BaseHook):
+    """Hook SimpleCPUOffloadWorker to skip CUDA and auto-complete transfers."""
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "SimpleCPUOffloadWorker"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.v1.simple_kv_offload.worker"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        def override_init(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            """Skip pinned memory and CUDA streams."""
+            self._connector_metadata = None
+            self._completed_store_events: dict[int, int] = {}
+            logger.info(
+                "[vLLM Hijack] SimpleCPUOffloadWorker.__init__: "
+                "skipped CUDA allocation (simulation mode)"
+            )
+
+        def override_register_kv_caches(self, kv_caches):
+            """No-op: no actual KV cache tensors to register."""
+            pass
+
+        def override_bind_connector_metadata(self, metadata):
+            """Keep the metadata without tracking CUDA events."""
+            self._connector_metadata = metadata
+
+        def override_handle_preemptions(self, kv_connector_metadata):
+            """No-op: no in-flight transfers to flush."""
+            pass
+
+        def override_start_load_kv(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            """No-op: loads auto-complete via override_get_finished."""
+            pass
+
+        def override_wait_for_save(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            """No-op: stores auto-complete via override_get_finished."""
+            pass
+
+        def override_get_finished(self, finished_req_ids):
+            """Report all loads finished and the store event completed.
+
+            Returns (finished_sending, finished_recving).
+            """
+            meta = self._connector_metadata
+            finished_recving = set()
+
+            if meta is not None and meta.load_event >= 0:
+                for reqs in meta.load_event_to_reqs.values():
+                    finished_recving.update(reqs)
+
+            if meta is not None and meta.store_event >= 0:
+                self._completed_store_events[meta.store_event] = 1
+
+            return None, finished_recving or None
+
+        target.__init__ = override_init
+        target.register_kv_caches = override_register_kv_caches
+        target.bind_connector_metadata = override_bind_connector_metadata
+        target.handle_preemptions = override_handle_preemptions
+        target.start_load_kv = override_start_load_kv
+        target.wait_for_save = override_wait_for_save
+        target.get_finished = override_get_finished
+
+
+class C_VLLMOffloadingConnectorWorkerHook(BaseHook):
+    """Hook OffloadingConnectorWorker to auto-complete transfers.
+
+    The native __init__ creates no CUDA resources; the transfer worker is
+    built in register_kv_caches, which is skipped here.
+    """
+
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "OffloadingConnectorWorker"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.worker"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        def override_register_kv_caches(self, kv_caches):
+            """No-op: keeps the transfer worker unbuilt."""
+            pass
+
+        def override_handle_preemptions(self, kv_connector_metadata):
+            """No-op: no in-flight transfers to flush."""
+            pass
+
+        def override_start_kv_transfers(self, metadata):
+            """Record load jobs; get_finished completes them."""
+            for job_id, entry in metadata.load_jobs.items():
+                self._load_jobs[job_id] = entry.req_id
+
+        def override_prepare_store_kv(self, metadata):
+            """Mark store jobs completed immediately."""
+            for job_id in metadata.store_jobs:
+                self._connector_worker_meta.mark_completed(job_id)
+
+        def override_get_finished(self, finished_req_ids):
+            """Report all loads as immediately finished."""
+            finished_recving: set[str] = set()
+            for job_id, req_id in self._load_jobs.items():
+                self._connector_worker_meta.mark_completed(job_id)
+                finished_recving.add(req_id)
+            self._load_jobs.clear()
+            return set(), finished_recving
+
+        target.register_kv_caches = override_register_kv_caches
+        target.handle_preemptions = override_handle_preemptions
+        target.start_kv_transfers = override_start_kv_transfers
+        target.prepare_store_kv = override_prepare_store_kv
+        target.get_finished = override_get_finished

+"""
+CPU stand-in for GPUModelRunnerV2 (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py),
+driven by the native Worker.
+
+KV tensors are one page each; page sizes stay at real model values since
+they are accounting-only.
+"""
+
+import functools
+import os
+
+import torch
+from torch.overrides import TorchFunctionMode
+
+from vllm_simulator.simulation.manager import ConfigManager
+from vllm_simulator.utils import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+def _noop(*args, **kwargs):
+    """Module-level so it is picklable."""
+    return None
+
+
+class _ModelRunnerStub:
+    """Picklable model_runner stub; other attributes resolve to no-ops."""
+
+    # Read by Worker.execute_model under the V2 runner.
+    is_pooling_model = False
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config, kv_spec: dict):
+        from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.kv_connector import NO_OP_KV_CONNECTOR
+
+        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self._kv_spec = kv_spec
+        self.kv_connector = NO_OP_KV_CONNECTOR
+        self.model_memory_usage = 0
+        # Explicit None (not the __getattr__ no-op) so LLMEngine skips its
+        # model cleanup finalizer.
+        self.model = None
+

+        return self._kv_spec
+

+        return ("generate",)

+        """Allocate one-page CPU KV tensors and hand them to the V2 KV
+        connector wrapper."""
+        from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.kv_connector import get_kv_connector
+
+        kv_caches: dict = {}
+        for kv_tensor in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors:
+            tensor = torch.zeros(
+                min(kv_tensor.size, 4096), dtype=torch.int8, device="cpu"
+            )
+            for layer_name in kv_tensor.layers:
+                kv_caches[layer_name] = tensor
+        logger.info(
+            "[vLLM Hijack] Allocated %d MINIMAL CPU KV cache tensors "
+            "(num_blocks=%d, simulated_bytes=%d, actual_bytes=4k)",
+            len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors),
+            kv_cache_config.num_blocks,
+            sum(t.size for t in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors),
+        )
+        self.kv_connector = get_kv_connector(self.vllm_config, kv_caches)
+
+    def execute_model(self, scheduler_output, intermediate_tensors=None):
+        """Mock forward inside the V2 KV connector lifecycle.
+
+        Returns the output directly (no sample_tokens RPC); finish_forward
+        is skipped since only HiSparse connectors implement it.
+        """
+        from vllm.v1.outputs import ModelRunnerOutput
+
+        if not scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens:
+            return self.kv_connector.no_forward(scheduler_output)
+
+        self.kv_connector.pre_forward(scheduler_output)
+        kv_connector_output = self.kv_connector.post_forward(
+            scheduler_output.finished_req_ids
+        )
+
+        # Whether each request samples a token this step comes from
+        # C_VLLMExecutorHook (_sim_token_emitted).
+        req_ids = list(scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens)
+        token_emitted = scheduler_output._sim_token_emitted
+        return ModelRunnerOutput(
+            req_ids=req_ids,
+            req_id_to_index={rid: i for i, rid in enumerate(req_ids)},
+            sampled_token_ids=[

+            ],
+            kv_connector_output=kv_connector_output,
+        )

+    def __getattr__(self, name):

+
+class _ForceMetaDevice(TorchFunctionMode):
+    """Redirect explicit ``device=`` arguments to meta; the plain
+    ``torch.device("meta")`` context only fills in a missing device."""
+
+    def __torch_function__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        kwargs = kwargs or {}
+        if kwargs.get("device") is not None:
+            kwargs["device"] = "meta"

+class _NullCudaStream:

+    the meta build."""

+        pass
+
